supporting_observations.claim: At 13:43:25 UTC, a successful network logon to WS-AHASSAN-01 targeted ali.hassan, with WS-NKIM-01 and 10.53.10.22 recorded as the source. This is shortly after the alert time and is atypical given the supplied inventory that remote administration is only performed from WS-AHASSAN-01; the record does not establish that this logon was related to creating helpdesk2.
WS-NKIM-01 made Kerberos and SMB connections to the domain controller shortly before the alert, but these flow records do not identify the accounts or operations involved.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided records include network-flow metadata and a Windows 4624 logon event, but no domain-controller account-management event or process/command telemetry confirming an account creation. The nearby Kerberos and SMB records do not expose the actions performed. (T147-00114, T147-00118, T147-00127)
claims_not_established: Whether helpdesk2 was actually created, and the precise creation time, actor, and originating host.
Whether the ali.hassan network logon from WS-NKIM-01 was connected to the alert or authorized.
Whether helpdesk2 was added to any groups or granted privileges.
Who was operating WS-NKIM-01 at the time.
additional_evidence_needed: Domain-controller security and directory audit events for the alert window, especially account creation, group membership changes, and the associated subject, logon ID, and source.
Endpoint process and command-line telemetry from WS-NKIM-01 and WS-AHASSAN-01 around 13:42–13:44 UTC.
Authentication and session details that can link or rule out the 13:43:25 ali.hassan logon from WS-NKIM-01 to the account-management alert.
The helpdesk2 account's current and historical group memberships, enabled status, and creation attributes.
unrelated_findings: WS-NKIM-01 accessed a Google Docs document and made a connection to Google Drive, services outside the supplied approved-services list. Track separately; this does not establish who created helpdesk2. (T147-00242, T147-00243, T147-00295)
